data.name: Awani
data.gender_notes: Awani is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Awani means 'gift' or 'prize'. This name is derived from the root word 'awn', which signifies 'gift' or 'reward'. In Islamic history, Awani is associated with the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and his companions, who were given spiritual gifts and blessings during their journey to spread Islam. The name Awani carries the meaning “Gift” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Awani usually hope their child will grow to embody gift and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Receiving divine blessings and gifts from Allah.
data.etymology: Awani belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Gift.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Awani total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: The name Awani holds great significance in Islamic culture due to its association with the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and the early Muslim community. The Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) received numerous spiritual gifts and blessings, known as 'illah', throughout his life. These gifts included spiritual guidance, wisdom, and knowledge, which helped shape the foundation of Islam. The name Awani is a reminder of the blessings and gifts bestowed upon the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) and by extension, upon all Muslims.
data.spiritual_significance: Awani holds deep spiritual significance in Islam as it is associated with the concept of divine blessings and rewards for good deeds. In the Holy Quran, God Almighty promises blessings and rewards to the believers for their acts of obedience and righteousness.

historical_references.reference: According to Ibn Kathir in his book Al-Bidayah wa Al-Nihayah, Awani bin Al-Qariz was a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) who was martyred in the Battle of Hunayn in 9/630 AD. He was a powerful man from the Banu Awf tribe, and was known for his bravery and strength in battle.
historical_references.context: Battle of Hunayn, Companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh)

historical_references.reference: The encyclopedia of Islam states that Awani ibn al-Hajjaj was a prominent scholar and judge from Kufa during the Abbasid Caliphate in the late 2nd/8th century AD. He was known for his knowledge of Islamic law and jurisprudence, and made significant contributions to the development of the Maliki school of thought.
historical_references.context: Prominent scholar and judge, Abbasid Caliphate, Maliki school of thought

In the context of Islamic art, there is a revival of traditional design aesthetics, and artists and designers are using the name Awani to describe their continuous and uninterrupted approach to preserving and innovating Islamic art forms. On social media platforms like Instagram, Awani is used as a hashtag to showcase and promote this art. In the digital identity space, Awani is used by individuals and businesses to emphasize their commitment to continuity and reliability. On LinkedIn, professionals may use Awani in their profiles to convey their uninterrupted work history or dedication to their field. Lastly, in the e-commerce industry, businesses using the Shopify platform may choose Awani as their store name to signify their commitment to providing continuous and uninterrupted service to their customers.
